summary: Agricola is a dense worker-placement engine-builder where you juggle a constant tug-of-war between growing your family, farming, and building a house, all while a harvest clock forces you to feed everyone or suffer penalties. Games are tense, calculation-heavy, and reward efficient long-term planning over reactive play.
praised: Deep, satisfying engine-building with many viable strategies
The revised edition's streamlined card decks and clearer rules make it more approachable than the original
High replayability from the occupation/minor improvement cards
Tight, tense resource management (the 'feed your family' pressure)
criticised: Can feel punishing or fiddly for newer players, especially the food/begging penalty
Longer playtime and analysis paralysis in higher player counts
Card-drafting variability can create imbalance between players
Farm-building theme is thin; feels more like an abstract optimization puzzle to some

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial over shared action spaces

scoring.why: Points are totaled across fields, pastures, animals, house type, family size, and card bonuses, so a balanced farm usually beats a one-track strategy
